archive.context: A filing cabinet with three pull-out drawers. Used for archive actions in email and document apps, record storage, office filing and older items moved out of the main view.

archive-box.context: Storage box with a lid and a hand slot cut into the side. Shows up on archive buttons, moving items to long-term storage, boxed records and storage or moving services.

blueprint.context: An architectural floor plan drawn on a sheet, with walls and a door swing. Used for architecture and construction apps, property listings, building plans and site planning documents.

book.context: Closed hardcover book seen from the front. Used for reading apps, libraries, guides, manuals, education platforms and links to documentation.

book-open.context: An open book with two facing pages. Common on documentation links, reading modes, help centres, tutorials, study apps and e-reader views.

books.context: Three books lying flat in a pile. Used for reading lists, course materials, libraries, collections of guides and education or bookstore sections.

catalog.context: A catalogue booklet with a grid of products on the cover. Used for product catalogues, brochures, store listings, collections and browsing an inventory in shop apps.

certificate.context: Certificate sheet with a seal and ribbon at the bottom. Used for course completion, awards, diplomas, qualifications and accreditation pages in education and HR tools.

clipboard.context: An empty clipboard with a metal clip at the top. Used for copy and paste actions, forms, inspections, surveys and anything held on a board for review.

clipboard-list.context: Clipboard holding a bulleted list of items. Common in task managers, to-do lists, inventory checks, inspections and project checklists.

clipboard-text.context: A clipboard carrying several lines of text. Used for notes, memos, forms, briefs, meeting minutes, medical records and pasted text content.

contract.context: An agreement page with lines of text and a signature line marked with a cross. Used for contracts, terms and conditions, legal agreements, leases and places where someone must sign.

cover-page.context: Title page with a centred title and an author line below it. Used for report covers, book title pages, document templates and front matter in publishing tools.

document-signed.context: A document page with a handwritten signature on a line. Used to show signed or approved documents, completed e-signatures, executed contracts and consent forms.

dossier.context: Folder with papers sticking out and a label on the front. Used for case files, personnel records, confidential documents, investigations and client files.

envelope-document.context: An envelope with a letter sliding out of it. Used for mail, sending or receiving documents, correspondence, newsletters and attaching a document to a message.

file.context: Plain document page with a folded top corner. The general icon for a file, new document, page or attachment in file managers, editors and upload areas.

file-3d.context: Document page with a small cube on it, marking a 3D model file. Used in 3D printing, CAD, game asset and model viewer apps for mesh and scene files.

file-audio.context: A document page marked with a music note. Used for audio files, songs, recordings, podcasts and sound attachments in file lists and media libraries.

file-certificate.context: Document page with a seal and ribbon, meaning a certificate file. Used for downloadable certificates, diplomas, signed credentials and verified documents.

file-csv.context: A document page filled with rows of separated values. Used for CSV exports and imports, data downloads, contact lists and tabular data files.

file-database.context: Document page with a database cylinder on it. Used for database files, SQL dumps, backups, data sources and local stores in developer and admin tools.

file-document.context: A document page with a heading and paragraph lines, as used for word-processing files. Common for text documents, letters, essays, reports and doc attachments.

file-font.context: Document page with a letter A on it, meaning a font file. Used in type managers, design tools, font downloads and typography settings.

file-image.context: A document page showing a small picture of mountains and a sun. Used for image files, photo uploads, picture attachments and graphics in file lists.

file-invoice.context: Document page with item lines and amounts, meaning an invoice file. Used for billing, downloading invoices, payment records and accounting apps.

file-json.context: A document page with curly braces, meaning a JSON data file. Used for config files, API responses, data exports and settings in developer tools.

file-pdf.context: Document page with a picture block and lines of text, standing for a print-ready PDF. Used for PDF downloads, exports, printable forms, reports and attachments.

file-presentation.context: A document page with a slide on a small stand. Used for presentation files, slide decks, pitch decks and meeting materials.

file-report.context: Document page with a small line chart, meaning a report file. Used for analytics reports, monthly summaries, exported results and business documents.

file-shield.context: A document page with a shield on it, meaning a protected file. Used for encrypted or secured documents, privacy settings, restricted access and scanned-safe files.

file-spreadsheet.context: Document page divided into a grid of cells, used for spreadsheet files. Common in finance, data entry, budgets and table exports.

file-stack.context: Two document pages stacked one over the other. Used for multiple files, batch uploads, copies, duplicate documents and selecting several items at once.

file-text.context: A document page with lines of plain text. Used for text files, notes, logs, readme files, transcripts and plain-text attachments.

file-vector.context: Document page with a curve drawn between two anchor points, marking a vector graphic. Used for SVG and illustration files in design tools, logo downloads and print artwork.

file-video.context: A document page with a play triangle, meaning a video file. Used for video uploads, movie files, clips, recordings and media attachments.

file-zip.context: Document page with a zipper running down it, meaning a compressed archive. Used for zip downloads, compressing or extracting files and bundled attachments.

folder.context: A closed folder with a tab. The standard icon for directories, collections, projects and grouped files in file managers, cloud drives and sidebars.

folder-open.context: An open folder with its front flap tilted forward. Used for opening or browsing a directory, the current folder, file pickers and expanded tree items.

folder-shared.context: Folder with a person on it, meaning it is shared with others. Used for team drives, shared directories, collaboration spaces and access settings.

folder-tree.context: A parent folder branching down to two sub-folders. Used for folder hierarchies, directory trees, nested files, sidebars and project structure views.

folder-zip.context: A folder with a zipper on the front, meaning a compressed folder. Used for zipping a directory, downloading a whole folder and archived project files.

folders.context: Two folders, one behind the other. Used for multiple directories, collections, grouped projects, moving several folders and library sections.

id-card.context: Identity card with a portrait on one side and detail lines on the other. Used for ID verification, profiles, membership cards, contact details and driving licences.

inbox.context: A tray with an arrow pointing down into it, meaning incoming items. Used for email inboxes, received messages, notifications, requests and download destinations.

invoice.context: Invoice sheet with a header block, item lines and a total at the bottom. Used for billing pages, sending invoices, payments due, accounting and order summaries.

journal.context: A journal closed with an elastic strap and a ribbon bookmark. Used for diary and journaling apps, planners, logs, personal notes and reflections.

library.context: A shelf of standing books with one book leaning over. Used for library sections, collections of saved items, media libraries, study resources and reading apps.

magazine.context: Magazine cover with a masthead title and a portrait. Used for publications, news and lifestyle apps, digital editions, subscriptions and editorial content.

manuscript.context: A handwritten page covered in wavy lines of script. Used for drafts, handwriting, original writing, author tools, calligraphy and historical documents.

newspaper.context: A folded newspaper with a headline photo and text columns. Used for news feeds, articles, press pages, blogs, media coverage and daily briefings.

note.context: A notepad sheet with binding rings along the top and ruled lines. Used for notes apps, memos, quick jotting, reminders and adding a note to a record.

notebook.context: A spiral-bound notebook with a coil down the spine. Used for notes, school and study apps, exercise books, sketching and writing workspaces.

notes.context: Two overlapping notes, the front one lined with text. Used for note collections, memos, annotations, meeting notes and multiple saved notes.

outbox.context: A tray with an arrow pointing up out of it, meaning outgoing items. Used for sent mail, outgoing messages, queued uploads and exports.

page-blank.context: A blank sheet of paper with nothing on it. Used for new documents, empty pages, blank templates, starting from scratch and empty states.

pages.context: Two sheets of paper, the back one tilted behind the front. Used for multiple pages, page lists in site builders, copies, document sets and stacks of paperwork.

paperclip.context: A single paperclip on its side. The standard icon for attachments, attaching a file to an email or message, clipped documents and office supplies.

passport.context: A passport booklet with a globe emblem on the cover. Used for travel apps, identity verification, visa and border pages, bookings and citizenship forms.

receipt.context: A paper receipt with a torn zigzag bottom edge. Used for purchase history, order confirmations, payments, expenses and proof of purchase in shop and finance apps.

report.context: Report sheet with a title line and a small bar chart. Used for business reports, analysis results, reviews, summaries and generated report pages.

scroll.context: A parchment scroll rolled at the top and bottom. Used for ancient or historical documents, decrees, terms, legends, quests in games and formal proclamations.

sticky-note.context: A square sticky note with one corner folded up. Used for quick notes, reminders, whiteboard and brainstorming apps, pinned comments and annotations.

table-of-contents.context: A page listing entries with page numbers on the right. Used for tables of contents, document outlines, chapter lists, indexes and in-page navigation.

ticket.context: An admission ticket with notches on each side and a tear line. Used for events, concerts, cinema bookings, passes, coupons, raffles and support tickets.
